statements.text: Understandably, the cost of designing, training, and deploying AI is top-of-mind for any organization. Has the Department considered how it can leverage its existing technological capabilities –including on-premise, private cloud, public cloud, and hybrid cloud computing capabilities to design, train, and deploy AI in a manner that ensures compatibility with existing investments?
statements.venue: House Armed Services CITI subcommittee hearing, 'The Technology and AI Fight for 21st-Century Operations in the Department of Defense' (questions submitted by Mr. Strong)

statements.text: I commend FTI on its expansion in Huntsville, Alabama. The HACS Center will contribute to our national security through cyber security, data analytics and artificial intelligence. [...] Now more than ever, it's crucial the United States is on the cutting edge of next-generation war fighting and this investment will contribute to that mission.
statements.venue: Quoted in FTI/Huntsville Business Journal article on HACS Center expansion

statements.text: I know of several technology companies in my hometown of Huntsville that are in fact developing cyber defense technologies using AI. For instance, to address the Space and Missile Defense Command (SMDC)'s Space & Ground Systems operational cyber threat detection and prevention requirements and support the zero-trust strategy, technology is being developed to auto-configure, self-optimize, and self-train defensive models to detect and mitigate cyber threats against critical ground systems and space assets.
statements.context: House Armed Services Committee hearing on AI and cyber operations in the Department of Defense.

statements.text: The generative AI use case in particular is driving the need for increased compute availability. The compute available today is insufficient to satiate demand, nor agile enough with scale to respond to what's easily knowable and foreseeable on the horizon.
statements.context: Written testimony from a DoD official responding to a congressional hearing question about AI compute and cloud infrastructure for the Department of Defense.

statements.text: Advancements in emerging technologies like artificial intelligence and quantum computing are critical to our national security industry and our service branches. Through the Davidson and D-Wave partnership, we will be able to address the important needs of our military by using cutting edge technology and applications that are developed in the U.S.
statements.venue: D-Wave/Davidson Technologies press release (Space and Missile Defense Symposium)

statements.text: Advance the system to implement Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning to improve efficiency of responding. [...] Alabama A&M AI/ML are experienced in the development of algorithms from data collected to advance the protection operation from threats and make it more efficient.
statements.context: Written responses to questions from a House hearing on agroterrorism threats to the food supply chain.

statements.text: New technologies like AI and quantum computing could be critical to keeping our nation safe. I'm proud to see Davidson Technologies and D-Wave working together to bring this advanced system to Alabama, helping develop tools that support our military now and for years to come.

one concern is that AI allows adversaries to scale operations without scaling personnel. [...] When AI tools are misused by cyber activity what visibility, if any, does DHS and CISA have into these incidents?
statements.context: Congressional hearing on quantum, AI, and cloud cybersecurity, with a member questioning witnesses about DHS and CISA visibility into AI-enabled cyber threats.
